mappings.note: Assertion-reason on copper displacing iron -- false because copper is below iron. Tests the series as a predictor of displacement, LO-2.
Draws the reactivity series (LO-2) and annotates each region with what it implies for how that metal is extracted (LO-6). Both are genuinely demanded by the answer.
'Design and describe an experiment' establishing the order of Zn, Fe and Cu, with each metal in its own salt as a control. C 8.2-LO-2 word for word; LO-2 is the content it establishes.
Strong heating of a sulphide ore in air = roasting. Extraction step, LO-6.
True/false trap swapping calcination for roasting on a sulphide ore. Extraction step, LO-6.
When ionic compounds conduct (molten or dissolved). Consequence of ionic bonding -- the C 1.1 competency; no LO reaches ionic properties.
Why ionic melting points are high (strong lattice forces). Same competency as the other ionic-structure items.
Assertion-reason on solid NaCl conducting -- false because the ions are locked in the lattice. Ionic structure, C 1.1.
Derives every physical property of ionic compounds from the lattice. The fullest statement of the C 1.1 compound-formation competency in this chapter.
Al2O3 reacting with both acid and alkali means amphoteric. Oxide nature, the chemical property LO-1 classifies on.
True/false on all metal oxides being basic -- tests the amphoteric exception. LO-1.
Impure copper serves as the anode. Refining step of LO-6.
Labelled refining cell showing where pure copper deposits. Refining step of LO-6; the drawing is a recall diagram, not an investigation, so C 8.2 is not cited.
Why sodium is kept under kerosene -- it is at the top of the series and attacks air and moisture. LO-2.
Surveys metal reactions with oxygen, water and dilute acids. The graded vigour across metals is LO-2; the basic character of the oxides formed is LO-1.
Mineral versus ore. Ore vocabulary of LO-6.
Gangue is the earthy impurity. Concentration step of LO-6.
Percentage of metal in an ore sample. Numerical, but the context is ore grade, which belongs to LO-6; the frame has no quantitative outcome to cite instead.
Silver tarnishing to Ag2S in air. Corrosion, LO-7.
Corrosion defined, costed and prevented. LO-7 in full.
Definition of galvanisation, which LO-7 names explicitly.
Compares four rust-prevention methods including galvanisation and alloying. LO-7 exactly.

Why a scratched galvanised sheet still resists rust. The claim is corrosion prevention (LO-7) and the reason offered is that zinc outranks iron, which is LO-2 -- the item only works if the student holds both.
Matches galvanisation, tinning, painting and stainless steel to their agents. Corrosion prevention, LO-7.
Why carbon cannot reduce the oxides of highly reactive metals, so electrolysis is used. The high-reactivity branch of LO-6.
Ties extraction method to series position. LO-6 owns the extraction routes; LO-2 owns the series that decides between them, and the question is precisely the link.
Zinc blende to zinc: concentration, roasting, reduction, refining. The moderate-reactivity branch of LO-6.
Copper recovered from 2000 tonnes of 3 per cent ore at 90 per cent recovery. Ore-grade arithmetic under LO-6, as with 706982.
Why Na and Cl combine one to one. Valency and electron transfer, the C 1.1 competency.
Formation of the Mg-Cl ionic bond and deduction of MgCl2. Compound formation from atomic structure and valency, C 1.1.
The three stages of metallurgy: concentration, reduction, refining. LO-6's whole scope.

Three-tube experiment isolating air and water as the conditions for rusting. Content is corrosion (LO-7); the controlled design is inquiry, cited at C 8.2 because its LO is limited to comparing two metals' reactivity.
Mass gained by a rusting nail, as a percentage, and where the extra mass came from. Corrosion, LO-7; the arithmetic has no separate outcome.
